meaning:
δέρω
[in LXX: Lev.1:6, 2Ch.29:34; 35:11 (פָּשַׁט hi.)* ;]
1. to skin, flay.
2. (of. Eng. slang, hide) to beat, thrash: with accusative, Mat.21:35, Mrk.12:3, 5, Luk.20:10, 11 22:63, Jhn.18:23, Act.5:40 16:37 22:19; ὡς ἀέρα δέρων, 1Co.9:26; εἰς πρόσωπου δ., 2Co.11:20. Pass., Mrk.13:9, Luk.12:47, 48 (δαρήσεται πολλάς, ὀλίγας, Sc. πληγάς).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: The farmers took his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
They took him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
That servant, who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare, nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?”
They agreed with him. Summoning the apostles, they beat them and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
I therefore run like that, not aimlessly. I fight like that, not beating the air,
For you bear with a man if he brings you into bondage, if he devours you, if he takes you captive, if he exalts himself, or if he strikes you on the face.
